Proprietary in-house technology stack (supply-demand allocation engine, Frodo delivery-partner lifecycle system with UIDAI/NSDL touchless onboarding, SF Shield fraud detection with track-and-trace, SF Maps address intelligence, APIs for client integration) orchestrates the network. Forward extension into multi-brand dark store operations and strategic insourcing of unbundled supply-chain services; acquisition of 89.59% of Criticalog India Private Limited (November 22, 2024) added freight management, air and road express, freight forwarding, intermodal transportation, warehousing, customs house clearance, trade compliance and supply chain management capabilities.

internal_operational.detail: Business depends on a nationwide logistics network of touchpoints, sort centers and leased transport; equipment failures, force majeure, political disruptions, strikes or regulatory shutdowns can delay/suspend shipments, force rerouting, increase costs and breach delivery commitments. Past incidents: May 2024 shipment-sorter spare-part system failure at Bilaspur (Gurugram) forced rerouting via Jaipur, Lucknow and Surat causing breach of certain delivery time commitments; August 2024 shutdown of some facilities in Kolkata due to political disruptions.
internal_operational.evidence: As of September 30, 2025: 4,299 touchpoints; >3.50 million sq ft operational space; 14,758 pin codes; 90 first mile and return-to-seller centers, 53 middle-mile sortation centers, 4,156 last-mile centers (incl. franchisee); all trucks/LCVs leased from third-party fleet partners. Capex additions to logistics facilities: H1 FY26 Rs 496.11 mn (80.26% of total capex), H1 FY25 Rs 114.90 mn (47.96%), FY2025 Rs 461.53 mn (66.31%), FY2024 Rs 409.32 mn (77.06%), FY2023 Rs 411.36 mn (87.05%)
internal_operational.title: Reliance on scaled unified network infrastructure; disruption risk

internal_operational.detail: Heavy reliance on key commercial relationships; loss or reduction of business from key clients (Meesho, Flipkart, Zepto, Kartrocket, Zomato named among top customers), demand for more favourable terms, or non-renewal of contracts could materially impact revenue and profitability. Group Companies (Flipkart entities) contributed more than 10% of revenue in certain periods.
internal_operational.title: Client concentration: largest client ~48-60% of revenue

internal_operational.detail: A large flexible gig delivery-partner network is instrumental to success; partners are non-exclusive, may migrate to competing or ride-hailing platforms based on incentives, and supply constraints have occurred in the past (not material). Attrition in the gig workforce, incentive escalation, gig-worker labour-law costs, and coordinated protests/strikes could disrupt operations.
internal_operational.evidence: 205,864 Average Quarterly Unique Transacting Delivery Partners as of September 30, 2025 (H1 FY25: 1,24,132; FY2025: 1,51,385; FY2024: 101,761; FY2023: 140,468). India gig workers expected to rise to ~24 million by FY2030 (RedSeer). Largest crowdsourced last-mile delivery fleet among 3PL e-commerce players by average monthly transacting riders (FY2025 and H1 FY26, RedSeer)

concerns_observed: Client concentration: largest client contributed 48.91% of revenue in H1 FY26 (48.00% FY25, 59.23% FY24, 59.52% FY23); top-10 clients 84.32% in H1 FY26 (90.74% FY24, 92.12% FY23).

Related-party revenue: Group company Instakart Services contributed Rs 2,668.57 million / 10.74% of revenue in FY2025 and Rs 2,191.67 million / 12.14% in H1 FY26; Flipkart entities are both group companies and a Selling Shareholder.
Thin profitability and return ratios despite the turnaround: RoNW 0.97% in FY2025 (from -80.90% FY23, -2.82% FY24) and 3.03% in H1 FY26; FY2025 basic EPS Rs 0.13.

Gig-workforce dependence with non-exclusive partners and high attrition: total workforce attrition 50.21% in FY2025 (contractual 58.69%); partners can migrate to competing/ride-hailing platforms on incentives.

Entire growth capex is quotation-based with no orders placed (Rs 4,234.31 million machinery table, order_placed false throughout) and the fund deployment has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.

Cash-on-delivery cash-handling exposure: 11 Section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act complaints and 71 FIRs against franchisees/hub in-charges/delivery partners for theft, swapping and robbery (aggregate pecuniary value ~Rs 32.00 million).
All logistics facilities are leased (short-term leases up to 11 months) exposing the company to renewal, rent-escalation and relocation risk.

Prior data breach in FY2023 during a back-up migration (customer mobile numbers and shipment tracking identifiers stolen); DPDP Act 2023 and new Labour Codes (effective November 21, 2025) raise compliance-cost exposure.
